title: The Bob Wilber album and George Duvivier
summary: Campbell praises Wilber and the 1969 album with Gus Johnson and Duvivier, whose Bass Fiddle bar he recalls.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Excuse me, who was the leader of the World's Greatest Jazz Band, a young boy, I don't know whether he was on an alto or tenor.
You mean he was with it. Bob Wilber?
Bob Wilber, he was sensational, yeah.
He and Maxine did a terrific album together.
My album, 'Closest Pages In A Book.'
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I got several, I've got on that --
Gus Johnson on drums. George Duvivier (phonetic spelling) on bass. You remember he had the bar and grill on 142nd and Avenue, the Bass Fiddle?
Yeah, he had a place there, oh, this was about 30 years ago. Well, that young man, Bob Wilber he impressed me to no heights, he was beautiful, he was driving me crazy.
